title: "Assignment 4: Polyglot Parity"
format: html

## Load data (relative path)

```{r}
library(dplyr)
nhanes <- read.csv("../../../examples/nhanes-equity/data/nhanes_equity_v6.csv")
nrow(nhanes)
```

## Filter: drop rows missing BMI or IncomeGroup

```{r}
analytic <- nhanes |> filter(!is.na(BMI), !is.na(IncomeGroup))
nrow(analytic)
```

## BMI summary by IncomeGroup and Gender

```{r}
analytic |>
  group_by(IncomeGroup, Gender) |>
  summarise(n = n(), mean_bmi = round(mean(BMI), 2),
            sd_bmi = round(sd(BMI), 2), median_bmi = round(median(BMI), 2),
            .groups = "drop") |>
  arrange(IncomeGroup, Gender)
```

## Reusable function

```{r}
summarise_bmi <- function(data) {
  data |>
    filter(!is.na(BMI), !is.na(IncomeGroup)) |>
    group_by(IncomeGroup, Gender) |>
    summarise(n = n(), mean_bmi = round(mean(BMI), 2),
              sd_bmi = round(sd(BMI), 2), median_bmi = round(median(BMI), 2),
              .groups = "drop") |>
    arrange(IncomeGroup, Gender)
}
summarise_bmi(nhanes)
```

## Parity discussion

Both languages use the same filter (drop missing BMI or IncomeGroup), the same groups, sample SD (n-1), and round to 2 decimals at the end. See parity-table.csv. To render: `quarto render polyglot-parity.qmd` from the submission folder.
